checks.name: zephyrSdkAvailableForHost
checks.detail: The Zephyr SDK publishes a host build for macos-aarch64.

checks.name: pythonFloor
checks.detail: no alp-sdk metadata/bootstrap.json was read (no SDK checkout resolved, or this SDK predates it), so tan's own built-in floor 3.10 is standing in, but the build's effective floor is 3.12 (from /home/dev/zephyrproject/zephyr/cmake/modules/python.cmake). Both `tan doctor` and `tan bootstrap` enforce the higher, effective floor, so a host this manifest would have accepted is refused up front rather than failing later at Zephyr's CMake configure.
checks.fix: Resolve an alp-sdk checkout: get an alp-sdk checkout (`git clone https://github.com/alplabai/alp-sdk`), then point tan at it with `--sdk-root <path>`. That checkout's own metadata/bootstrap.json pythonMinVersion is then read instead of tan's built-in floor.

checks.name: hostPrerequisites
checks.detail: git, cmake, python3, ninja present (tan's built-in fallback list (no alp-sdk checkout resolved)).

checks.name: west
checks.detail: `west` is not on bare PATH, but resolves through the workspace venv: /home/dev/zephyrproject/.venv/bin/west -- the same binary `westResolved` above reports, and the one a real build actually spawns. This is the default state right after `tan bootstrap`, which deliberately does not put `west` on PATH; activating the venv (its `bin`/`Scripts` directory holds the `west` launcher) would additionally put it on bare PATH, for tools that spawn it directly rather than through tan.

checks.name: setools
checks.detail: AEN MRAM flashing over the SE-UART is Linux-only in this tree: scripts/west_commands/runners/alif_flash.py hard-codes `app-release-exec-linux`, so its bundle is `app-release-exec-linux-SE_FW_x.y.z`. Nothing to check on this host for THAT path -- run it from WSL2/Linux (Windows hosts pass the SE-UART through with usbipd). Flow D below is a different matter: it signs on Windows with the WINDOWS SETOOLS build, which is a different bundle from the `-linux` one named above -- point `--setools-dir` at it (measured: `app-gen-toc.exe` under a Windows `app-release-exec`, SETOOLS_version_SE_FW_1.110.00_DEV, signed an ATOC the part booted from).

checks.name: jlink
checks.detail: J-Link V9.26 (/usr/local/bin/JLinkExe) predates V9.46, which is where Alif's MRAM flash loader became built in -- Flow D has nothing to program MRAM with on this DLL. Flow D needs the `AE822FA0E5597LS0_M55_HE` part-number device profile (NOT the generic `Cortex-M55`, which has no MRAM loader) and a J-Link DLL V9.46+. Device profile resolved from: tan's built-in fallback AE822FA0E5597LS0_M55_HE -- no alp-sdk checkout resolved to read metadata/socs/alif/ensemble/e8.json variants[].debug.jlink_flash_device from.
checks.fix: Upgrade the SEGGER J-Link pack to V9.46+.
